title: Cyber appellate tribunal - does it even function anymore
p1: A cyber law body created to protect digital rights… but many people don't even know if it still exists. So, what happened to the Cyber Appellate Tribunal?
p2: A common misconception is that every specialised tribunal created by law continues to operate forever. The Cyber Appellate Tribunal was set up under the Information Technology Act to hear appeals against certain decisions of cyber authorities. But over time, vacancies, lack of appointments, and administrative changes affected its functioning. A surprising fact: its role was eventually transferred to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT), meaning the original tribunal stopped functioning as an independent forum.
p3: For ordinary users, this matters because cyber disputes involving online platforms, digital transactions, and regulatory decisions need a proper place for appeal. A right without an accessible remedy can become difficult to enforce. The lesson is simple: laws need active institutions behind them, not just words on paper.
conclusion: Do you think India needs a dedicated cyber tribunal again, or are existing forums enough to handle digital disputes?
